title: A recent evaluation on the performance of LLMs on radiation oncology physics using questions of randomly shuffled options

paper.authors: Wang, Holmes, Liu, Chen, Liu, Shen, Liu (Mayo Clinic Radiation Oncology)
paper.repo_note: Named in the Data Availability Statement (scaffold URL had 'Author' glued to it). It is the lab's general radiation-oncology NLP dataset repo (2023), not a paper-specific code release.

dependence.note: All results are LLM accuracies on the 100-question exam (5 option-shuffled trials, plus a 'None of the above' deductive-reasoning variant and an explain-first prompt variant). Humans are a majority vote from a prior study, not re-run.

claim.statement: All five evaluated LLMs (o1-preview, GPT-4o, LLaMA 3.1 405B, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) scored above 80% mean accuracy over five option-shuffled versions of the 100-question radiation oncology physics exam, with o1-preview (~94%) exceeding the medical-physicist majority vote and GPT-4o (~90%) second (Figure 1a; Discussion 4.1); replacing the correct option with 'None of the above' caused a steep drop for every model (Figure 3).
claim.metric: mean accuracy (%) over 5 shuffled trials +/- SD across trials; 100 MCQs (17 math-based); answer letter extracted from free-text responses by a locally hosted LLaMA 3.1 405B and manually verified

original_values.o1_preview_mean_pct: ~94 (Discussion 4.1 narrative; exact Figure-1 bar value not in extracted text)
original_values.gpt_4_turbo: NOT evaluated in this paper; 68.0% is a citation of the authors' prior TXIT study (ref 19)
original_values.nota_variant: all models 'much more poorly' (Figure 3; numbers only in figure)

claim.original_source: Figure 1 (bars, numeric values only in figure/Supplementary Material), Figure 3, Figure 4; Results 3.1-3.2; Discussion 4.1

protocol.model_note: BLOCKED - live model not an experimental arm. 'GPT-4-turbo' appears only in the Introduction as a cited prior result (68.0% on ACR TXIT). The experimental OpenAI arms were o1-preview (dead, 2025-07-28) and 'GPT-4o' whose snapshot is unspecified ('recently released version before September 30, 2024' - i.e. gpt-4o-2024-08-06 or gpt-4o-2024-05-13).
protocol.model_status: not applicable; possible re-scope to gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (dying 2026-10-23, in target list) or gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (not in target list)
protocol.endpoint: OpenAI chat completions (if re-scoped to GPT-4o); LLaMA 3.1 405B was self-hosted
protocol.prompt_source: Methods 2.1, verbatim: 'Please solve this radiation oncology physics problem: [radiation oncology physics problem].' ; Methods 2.2.2 explain-first/step-by-step prompt verbatim

params.temperature_note: 0.1 for all LLMs except o1-preview (fixed at 1); chosen instead of 0 because of cross-vendor semantics
params.seed: not reported (shuffle seeds for the five exam sets not published)
params.other: each question queried individually through the vendor API; all models 'recently released before 2024-09-30'

protocol.samples_note: five trials = five independently shuffled option orders, one query each; mean +/- SD over trials is the paper's sampling scheme (use instead of 3 seeds)
protocol.evaluation: Answer-letter extraction from free-form output by a self-hosted LLaMA 3.1 405B, followed by manual verification; accuracy vs. answer key; per-topic and math-subset breakdowns; human reference = majority vote of 9 medical physicists from the prior study

artifacts.prompts_note: prompts are verbatim in the paper
artifacts.data_path: 5-Question and answering (QA)/Medical-Physics-100questions-QA-format.csv (100 questions x options, correct flag) and '5-Question and answering (QA)/Radiation Physics Questions for ChatGPT.txt'
artifacts.eval_note: shuffling, 'None of the above' replacement and answer-extraction scripts are not in the repo
artifacts.notes: Exam authored by a Mayo medical physicist following the ABR study guide; 2 of 100 items have an option E. Frontiers Supplementary Material (not fetched) holds the option-position distribution and probably the per-model numbers.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: gpt-4-turbo is only cited from prior work; experimental OpenAI arms were o1-preview (dead) and GPT-4o (snapshot unspecified)
per-model numeric results are only in Figure 1/3 bars and Supplementary Material, not in the text
option-shuffle seeds and NOTA-replacement code not published, so the five exam sets cannot be regenerated identically
answer extraction used a self-hosted LLaMA 3.1 405B plus manual verification

baseline_alive.alternative: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as an unverifiable proxy for 'GPT-4o' (dying 2026-10-23)

budget.assumptions: CONDITIONAL re-scope to GPT-4o, short-prompt shuffled condition only: 100 items x 5 shuffles; ~220 in / ~450 out tokens. Adding the NOTA condition doubles it (~USD 7.8); the explain-first condition was not run for GPT-4o beyond a 1% check.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (only if re-scoped): survival if the GPT-4o mean accuracy over 5 shuffles lies within the original Figure-1 value +/- 2 SD (bootstrap over 100 items) and stays > 80%; direction of the NOTA claim (shuffled >> NOTA accuracy) must hold.
judgment.notes: Original values must first be read off Figure 1 / Supplementary Material; the text gives only ~90% (GPT-4o) and ~94% (o1-preview).

user_checks: Re-scope the card from gpt-4-turbo (only cited) to GPT-4o? If yes, which snapshot: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (in target_models) or gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (the likely 'latest before 2024-09-30', not in target_models)?
Obtain the exact per-model Figure-1 values from the Frontiers Supplementary Material before freezing original_values.

domain_notes: The 100-item exam follows the ABR radiation-physics study guide (12 basic physics, 10 measurements, 20 treatment planning, 17 imaging, 13 brachytherapy, 16 advanced planning, 12 safety/QA; 17 math-based). Shuffling options mitigates contamination from the previously published exam; commonly missed items (14, 27, 42, 67, 87, 95, 96) concern clinical medical-physics practice (AAPM TG reports), not calculation. The 'None of the above' variant was deliberately not given to humans, so it has no human reference.
